newsitem.title: USA: Insured losses from storms estimated at $265 mln.
newsitem.headline: Insured losses from storms estimated at $265 mln.

text.p: Insured property losses from storms that struck a seven-state region of the United States in late February and early March were estimated at $265 million, an industry trade group said.

Property Claim Services, an industry-supported group that tracks insurance losses, said states affected by the severe weather included Texas, Arkansas, Mississippi, Kentucky, Tennessee, Ohio and West Virginia.
PCS said it expects 135,500 claims will be filed in the affected areas.
In Texas, high winds and large hail swept through the south and central parts of the state.
Tornadoes and high winds caused damage in Arkansas and Mississippi.
Thunderstorm-related wind and rain caused damage across wide areas in Kentucky. Wind, hail and a tornado damaged property in Tennessee.
Ohio and West Virginia suffered damage from torrential rains.
